answer: License one mushroom plot per applicant on a shale slope for 120 days. Each pays a 150 token deposit and a 90 dollar license, then tags 40 beds with rings. A yarrow patch at the edge marks the plot, photographed weekly beside the basket. A zephyr gauge logs noon wind next to the weighed harvest, and a neighbor signs the tally. A forged tally forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 plots freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A cheat faces a poacher counting deer in a fenced wood where every animal wears a tag, and one missing tag empties the pen.
